findings.title: Hardcoded Django secret key and SantimPay private key in source
findings.why: Cryptographic secrets are committed in source control, enabling key theft and token/signature forgery.
findings.impact: Account/session compromise, payment signature forgery, and total environment compromise if reused across envs.
findings.scenario: An attacker with repo read access uses leaked private key to sign malicious SantimPay requests and impersonate trusted payment operations.
findings.fix: Move all secrets to environment/secret manager; fail fast if missing; rotate leaked keys immediately.

findings.title: Insecure production defaults (DEBUG=True, ALLOWED_HOSTS empty, missing secure headers)
findings.why: Debug mode and weak host/origin hardening expose stack traces and weaken host header protections.
findings.impact: Information disclosure, easier exploit development, cache poisoning/host-header abuse in misconfigured deployments.
findings.scenario: A production deployment forgets env overrides; attacker triggers errors to harvest secrets/config and internal paths.
findings.fix: Default to secure production posture with DEBUG=False, strict ALLOWED_HOSTS/CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS/CORS allowlist and HSTS/security headers.
findings.secure_example:
DEBUG = os.getenv('DEBUG','false').lower()=='true'
if not DEBUG:
    SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS=31536000
    SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=True
    CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE=True

findings.title: Broken object-level authorization on user profile endpoint
findings.why: No object-level permission checks ensure users can access only their own record.
findings.impact: IDOR allows viewing/updating/deleting arbitrary user accounts.
findings.scenario: Authenticated user requests /auth/user/<other-user-uuid>/ and edits victim profile or deletes account.
findings.fix: Restrict queryset to request.user or enforce IsSelfOrAdmin permission class.

findings.title: Authentication missing on critical order endpoints
findings.why: Views omit permission_classes, so API defaults may be bypassed/misapplied and business logic uses request.user directly.
findings.impact: Unauthorized order creation, cart checkout misuse, and data exposure if unauthenticated requests pass through with AnonymousUser edge cases.
findings.scenario: Attacker hits /order/create/ without token to stress order creation path and probe logic flaws; with middleware drift this becomes full auth bypass.
findings.fix: Explicitly set permission_classes=[IsAuthenticated] and validate authenticated user type before processing.

findings.title: Global data exposure due to missing ownership filters in CRUD endpoints
findings.snippet:
queryset = Shop.objects.all()
queryset = Inventory.objects...all()
queryset = Product.objects.all()
findings.why: List/detail/update/delete endpoints use unrestricted querysets with only IsAuthenticated, enabling cross-tenant read/write.
findings.impact: Multi-tenant isolation break: vendors can read/modify other vendors' shops, inventory, and products.
findings.scenario: Shop owner updates another shop by ID through ShopDetailView PATCH.
findings.fix: Filter by tenant ownership in get_queryset and enforce per-object permission checks.

findings.title: Unvalidated user-supplied notify_url in payment initiation (SSRF/webhook hijack)
findings.why: User-controlled callback URL is forwarded to payment provider without allowlisting.
findings.impact: SSRF-like callback abuse, exfiltration of transaction events to attacker-controlled endpoints, reconciliation tampering.
findings.scenario: Attacker sets notify_url to malicious endpoint and receives sensitive payment lifecycle callbacks.
findings.fix: Do not accept notify_url from client; use server-side configured callback or strict allowlist.

findings.title: Unsafe file upload controls missing (type/content scanning and size limits)
findings.why: No validators for extension/MIME/size or malware scanning pipeline are enforced.
findings.impact: Malicious file upload, storage abuse, possible XSS/content-sniffing issues when served, and legal/security risk.
findings.scenario: Attacker uploads polyglot HTML/SVG payload as product media and shares link for stored-XSS in weakly configured file serving.
findings.fix: Add strict file validators, max size, antivirus scanning, and safe content-disposition in media serving.

findings.title: No API throttling/rate-limiting on auth and transactional endpoints
findings.why: Missing throttle classes enables brute-force/login abuse and high-volume transaction abuse.
findings.impact: Credential stuffing, OTP/email abuse, DoS and fraud automation.
findings.scenario: Botnet sends massive login and payment-init requests without per-IP/user limits.
findings.fix: Enable DRF throttles plus edge rate-limits (Nginx/WAF/API gateway).

findings.title: Dependency/runtime misconfiguration risk: Django 6.0 pin likely incompatible
findings.why: Pinned version may be unreleased/incompatible with project assumptions; also requirements file appears UTF-16 encoded, harming tooling/scanners.
findings.impact: Broken deployments, missed vulnerability scanning, undefined runtime behavior.
findings.scenario: CI security scanner skips malformed requirements and misses vulnerable packages.
findings.fix: Use UTF-8 requirements, pin verified compatible versions, and run pip-audit/safety in CI.
findings.secure_example:
Django==5.1.*  # or tested LTS
# file encoded UTF-8

findings.title: Payment/refund business-logic race windows need stronger idempotency and locking
findings.why: Concurrent requests can create duplicate operational states without idempotency keys and select_for_update on critical rows.
findings.impact: Double-processing, inconsistent payout/refund accounting, financial reconciliation issues.
findings.scenario: Client retries quickly during timeout; two refund requests pass validation before status updates settle.
findings.fix: Introduce idempotency keys, unique constraints for active requests, and row-level locking around financial transitions.
